spots.name: Blackpool Tower
spots.summary: Blackpool Tower is a tourist attraction in Blackpool, Lancashire, England, which was opened to the public on 14 May 1894. When it opened, Blackpool Tower was the tallest man-made structure in the British Empire.

spots.name: Blackpool Pleasure Beach
spots.summary: Pleasure Beach Resort, best known by its former name Blackpool Pleasure Beach, is an amusement park situated on Blackpool's South Shore, in the county of Lancashire, North West England. The park was founded in 1896 by A. W. G. Bean and his partner John Outhwaite. The current managing director is Amanda Thompson.

spots.name: The Big One
spots.summary: The Big One is a steel hypercoaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. Designed by Ron Toomer and manufactured by Arrow Dynamics, the ride opened to the public on 28 May 1994 as the tallest roller coaster in the world, featuring a height of 65 metres.

spots.name: Big Dipper
spots.summary: Big Dipper is a wooden out-and-back roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. Originally built in 1923, its layout was extended in 1936. It was designated as a Grade II listed building on 19 April 2017.

spots.name: Infusion
spots.summary: Infusion is an inverted roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. It opened on 2 May 2007, and was built by Vekoma.

spots.name: North Pier
spots.summary: North Pier is the most northerly of the three coastal piers in Blackpool, England. Built in the 1860s, it is also the oldest and longest of the three. Although originally intended only as a promenade, competition forced the pier to widen its attractions to include theatres and bars.

spots.name: Winter Gardens
spots.summary: The Winter Gardens is a large entertainment complex in Blackpool, Lancashire, England, which includes a theatre, ballroom and conference facilities.

spots.name: Blackpool High Tide Organ
spots.summary: The High Tide Organ was a tidal organ 15 metres tall constructed in 2002 as part of "The Great Promenade Show" series of sculptures situated along Blackpool's New Promenade in the UK. It was removed in early 2022.

spots.name: Icon
spots.summary: Icon is a launched roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. Manufactured by Mack Rides, the ride opened on 25 May 2018, and had a total cost of £16.25 million.

spots.name: Revolution
spots.summary: Revolution is a launched shuttle roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. It was built by Arrow Development in 1979, and was the first European roller coaster to feature an inversion. Until the introduction of Infusion in 2007, it was the park's only inverting roller coaster.

spots.name: Avalanche
spots.summary: Avalanche is a steel bobsled roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. It was the first bobsled coaster in the United Kingdom, and remains the only one in the country. It was designed and built by Mack Rides and opened in 1988.

spots.name: Central Pier
spots.summary: Central Pier is one of three piers in the town of Blackpool, England, and was built in 1868.

spots.name: Blackpool Zoo
spots.summary: Blackpool Zoo is a 32-acre (13 ha) zoo, owned by Parques Reunidos and located in the sea-side resort of Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It cares for over 1,000 animals from all over the world.

spots.name: Wild Mouse
spots.summary: Wild Mouse was a Wooden roller coaster at Blackpool Pleasure Beach in Blackpool, England. It opened in 1958, and was one of only four remaining wooden wild mouse coasters left in the world during its final season of operation.

spots.name: Madame Tussauds Blackpool

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Madame Tussauds Blackpool is a wax museum located in Blackpool, United Kingdom. The attraction opened in 2011, replacing the previous Louis Tussauds Waxworks. It features over 80 wax figures of celebrities, film and television characters, athletes and musicians.

spots.name: Q7416048
spots.summary: Sandcastle Waterpark is an indoor waterpark with 18 water slides and other attractions in Blackpool, Lancashire, England.

spots.name: Nickelodeon Streak
spots.summary: Nickelodeon Streak is a wooden out-and-back roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. It was built in 1933 by Charles Paige, and utilizes the lift hill and other parts of the former Velvet Coaster, which was retired in 1932. The ride is an ACE Coaster Classic.

spots.name: Steeplechase
spots.summary: Steeplechase is a tri-tracked steel racing steeplechase roller coaster at Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England.

spots.name: Stanley Park
spots.summary: Stanley Park is a public park in the town of Blackpool on the Fylde coast in Lancashire, England. It is the town's primary park and covers an area of approximately 104 hectares. The park was designed to include significant sporting provisions, along with formal gardens, a boating lake and woodland area.

spots.name: Blue Flyer
spots.summary: Blue Flyer is a wooden roller coaster in the Nickelodeon Land section of Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England. It is believed to have been built by Charles Paige with assistance from Harry Traver. American Coaster Enthusiasts awarded the historic coaster its ACE Coaster Classic designation.

spots.name: Nickelodeon Land
spots.summary: Nickelodeon Land is a themed children's amusement section in Pleasure Beach Resort in Blackpool, England.

spots.name: St John's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The parish church of Blackpool Saint John the Evangelist, or St John's Blackpool, is an Anglican church in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It was completed in 1878 and is a Grade II listed building. A church was built on the site in 1821 and was replaced by the current building to accommodate a larger congregation.

spots.name: Empress Ballroom
spots.summary: The Empress Ballroom is an entertainment venue in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It is located within the Winter Gardens, a large entertainment complex in the town centre.

spots.name: Grand Theatre
spots.summary: Blackpool Grand Theatre, known locally as The Grand, is a theatre in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. Since 2006, it has also been known as the National Theatre of Variety. It is a Grade II* Listed Building.

spots.name: Opera House Theatre, Blackpool
spots.summary: The Opera House Theatre is a theatre in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It is located within the Winter Gardens, a large entertainment complex in the town centre and originally opened in 1889, although it has been rebuilt twice, in 1910 and 1939.

spots.name: Blackpool Promenade
spots.summary: Blackpool Promenade is a road and esplanade in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It runs for around 4 miles (6.4 km), from Queen's Promenade, at Gynn Square in the north, to a junction with Squires Gate Lane and Clifton Drive North, in the south. The promenade replaced a small parade which existed in the 1780s.

spots.name: Blackpool Town Hall
spots.summary: Blackpool Town Hall is a municipal building in Talbot Square, Blackpool, England. The town hall is the headquarters of Blackpool Council, which is the main governing body for the wider Borough of Blackpool. It is a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sacred Heart Church is a Roman Catholic church in Blackpool, Lancashire, England, on Talbot Road close to the town centre. It was the first Roman Catholic church built in Blackpool and has been designated a Grade II* listed building by English Heritage.

spots.name: St Chad's Church, Poulton-le-Fylde

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Chad's Church is an Anglican church in Poulton-le-Fylde, Lancashire, England. It is an active parish church in the Diocese of Blackburn and the archdeaconry of Lancaster. It is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II* listed building.

spots.name: South Pier
spots.summary: South Pier is one of three piers in Blackpool, England. Located on South Promenade on the South Shore, the pier contains a number of amusement and adrenaline rides. It opens each year from March to November and is owned by The Sedgwick family.

spots.name: Bloomfield Road
spots.summary: Bloomfield Road is a football stadium in Blackpool, Lancashire, England, which has been the home of Blackpool Football Club since 1901. It is the third stadium since the club's founding, the previous two being Raikes Hall Gardens and the Athletic Grounds.

spots.name: Grundy Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grundy is an art gallery located in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. Its eclectic programme consists of regional historic to recent contemporary art exhibitions. Opened in 1911, it is owned and operated by Blackpool Council.

spots.name: Beaver Creek
spots.summary: Beaver Creek was a children's amusement section in Pleasure Beach Resort. It initially opened in 1992, replacing the former children's section, Funshineland. It closed on 5 September 2010 when managing director Amanda Thompson announced that it would be replaced by Nickelodeon Land.

spots.name: St Anne's Church, St Anne's-on-the-Sea

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Anne's Church is the Anglican parish church of St Annes-on-the-Sea, a town on the Fylde coast in Lancashire, England. It is an active Church of England parish church in the Diocese of Blackburn and the archdeaconry of Lancaster.

spots.name: Blackpool Sands
spots.summary: Blackpool is a seaside town in Lancashire, England. It is located on the Irish Sea coast of the Fylde peninsula, approximately 27 miles (43 km) north of Liverpool and 14 miles (23 km) west of Preston. It is the main settlement in the borough of the same name.

spots.name: Miners' Convalescent Home
spots.summary: The Miners' Convalescent Home was a convalescent home for miners in the seaside resort of Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It was built in 1925–1927 for Lancashire and Cheshire miners and was opened by Edward, Prince of Wales. In 1995, English Heritage designated the home a Grade II listed building.

spots.name: Marsh Mill
spots.summary: Marsh Mill is an 18th-century tower windmill in Thornton, Lancashire, England. It was built in 1794 by Ralph Slater for local landowner Bold Hesketh. It functioned as a corn mill until the 1920s and has been fully restored.

spots.name: Little Marton Mill
spots.summary: Little Marton Mill is a 19th-century English tower windmill in Marton, Blackpool, Lancashire, England. It was built in 1838 by John Hays for grinding corn, and worked until 1928. It has been designated a Grade II listed building by Historic England.

spots.name: Poulton-le-Fylde War Memorial
spots.summary: Erected in 1921, the Poulton-le-Fylde War Memorial is located in the English market town of Poulton-le-Fylde, Lancashire. A Grade II listed structure, it stands in a small cobbled area at the north end of Market Place, having been moved from nearby Queen's Square in 1979.

spots.name: 1 Vicarage Road
spots.summary: 1 Vicarage Road is a Grade II listed building in the English market town of Poulton-le-Fylde, Lancashire. Built in 1839, it stands at the corner of Vicarage Road and Chapel Street. It directly across the latter from the Thatched House public house. Now an estate agent, the building was originally Poulton Savings Bank.

spots.name: Market Cross
spots.summary: Poulton-le-Fylde Market Cross, in the English market town of Poulton-le-Fylde, Lancashire, was likely erected in the 17th century. Standing at the southern end of Market Place, it is a Grade II listed structure.

spots.name: 4, 6 and 10, Queen Square
spots.summary: The White House is a historic building in the English market town of Poulton-le-Fylde, Lancashire. It has been designated a Grade II listed building by Historic England. The property is located in Queen's Square, around 250 feet (76 m) to the southeast of the town centre and Market Place.

spots.name: Jean Stansfield Memorial Park
spots.summary: Jean Stansfield Memorial Park is an urban children's park in the English market town of Poulton-le-Fylde. It is located on Station Road, at its junction with Vicarage Road, one of the main roads leading to and from the town centre.

spots.name: Thornton-Cleveleys War Memorial
spots.summary: Erected in 1923, the Thornton-Cleveleys War Memorial is located in Thornton-Cleveleys, Lancashire, England. A Grade II listed structure, it stands in a small garden in the southwestern corner of a junction known as Four Lane Ends.
